Optimal.Notes: The GoldSrc engine runs effortlessly at native resolution and high settings on the Deck; 6 W TDP is generous headroom for this era of game. A locked 60 fps gives a responsive feel that matters in this competitive shooter.

profiles.Summary: Counter-Strike (2000) is an extremely lightweight game by modern standards, and the Steam Deck's hardware vastly exceeds its minimum requirements, so it should run at a locked 60 fps with minimal effort. The main friction is likely compatibility and input configuration rather than performance, as the game predates modern controller support and relies on keyboard/mouse.
profiles.BasisNote: No Steam Deck-specific player reports were found; profiles are estimated from the game's extremely modest PC requirements (500 MHz CPU, 16 MB GPU) versus the Deck's vastly superior hardware. On first launch, confirm Proton compatibility and VAC status, set resolution manually if the game launches windowed, and configure a community controller layout since there is no native gamepad support.

MaxBattery.Notes: This 2000-era GoldSrc engine game needs almost no GPU power; a 4 W TDP and reduced GPU clock are more than sufficient. FSR upscaling from 960x600 keeps the display sharp while saving the little power the game does use.

KnownIssues: No native controller support — a keyboard/mouse layout or community controller config is required.
VAC (Valve Anti-Cheat) may cause issues or bans when running under Proton; verify VAC compatibility before playing online.
The game may default to a low resolution or windowed mode on first launch under Proton and may need manual resolution setting.
GoldSrc engine games can occasionally have audio crackling or missing sounds under Proton on Linux.

MaxPerformance.Notes: The GoldSrc engine will happily push hundreds of frames per second uncapped, but the LCD is limited to 60 Hz; uncapping allows the engine to run physics and input polling faster for marginally snappier feel. Battery life drops as the CPU/GPU are fully unleashed on a trivially light workload.

Optimal.Notes: The OLED's 90 Hz display is a great match for this lightweight engine; high textures and light AA look noticeably better with no meaningful performance cost. Still very power-efficient.
